author.name: Jannik Aßfalg
credits: Programs: Alesis Midiverb (1986), Keith Barr; machine semantics after Eric Brombaugh's MIT reverse engineering (emeb/MIDIVERB_RE) and the ROM layout documented by thement (thement/midiverb_emulator)

presentation.label: 1986 DIGITAL REVERB
presentation.summary: The Alesis Midiverb's own reverb programs, run at their original 16-bit arithmetic.
presentation.overview: Each program is the original unit's, read from its ROM and played step for step: the same delay lines, the same 12-bit input and the same rounding, at half rate like the original. This first build carries 24 Midiverb programs; the rest follow.
highlights: 24 original Midiverb programs: rooms, halls, gated and reverse
The original's grain: 12-bit input, 16-bit memory, its own rounding
usage: Choose MIDIVERB in FX2. PROG picks a program; changing it mutes the reverb for about 46 ms while its memory clears.
LEVL drives the 12-bit input: unity at 32, 64 is +6 dB; turn it down if the reverb crackles.
MIX on encoder F: 0 dry, 127 wet only.

controls.name: PROG
controls.doc: Midiverb program: decay in seconds, size, tone; gated and reverse

controls.name: LEVL
controls.doc: input level into the 12-bit converter: unity at 32, 64 is +6 dB

controls.name: MIX
controls.doc: dry/wet; 0 is exact dry, 127 wet only

limitations: Experimental: 24 Midiverb programs; not yet tested on a unit.
Costs about three times SPRING REV on the DSP in this build.
